newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank says no repo tender on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank says no repo tender on Wednesday.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said it would not hold a repo tender on Wednesday as market liquidity appeared sufficient.

"The liquidity now seems to be sufficient as the banking sector is very close to 100-percent fulfilment of its minimum reserves requirements (PMR)," said Peter Andresic, Head of the NBS Open Market Operation Department.
Andresic added that some 1.7 billion crowns will return to the sector on Wednesday from maturing state bonds. "This will compensate for the absence of our repo tender," he said.

The Slovak banking sector on Tuesday for the sixth time this year, and for the fifth time in a row, failed to meet its PMR, when banks deposited 99.91 percent of funds required by the NBS as minimum reserves.
But dealers have said most banks fulfilled their reserves requirements.
